stock_firmware: Afinia is Tiertime's rebrand (the profile was added by a Tiertime developer in OrcaSlicer PR #10705). It shares the same uncertainty as the Tiertime HS line: Klipper-style macros in the profile, firmware unconfirmed.
second_opinion: I could not disprove UNCLEAR, but the evidence for Klipper is stronger than the claim says. (1) PR #10705 was written by GitHub user GuoGeTiertime, who works at Tiertime. It adds only the H+1(HS) profiles (0.4 and 0.6 nozzle). The profile inherits fdm_afinia_common.json, which sets gcode_flavor "klipper" with PRINT_START EXTRUDER=/BED=, PRINT_END and PAUSE. That is the same as fdm_tiertime_common.json, so Afinia H+1(HS) is a Tiertime rebrand. It is probably the UP300HS or a close sibling, but I did not confirm that. (2) The part the researcher missed: the same Tiertime developer keeps an actively changed Klipper fork, GuoGeTiertime/klipper. It is 178 commits ahead of Klipper3d/klipper, was last pushed 2026-09-05, and has branches NewHX71X, Probe, ProbeAdjust, RealTimeGCode and camera. Its commits touch a filament feeder and print_stats (operate_flag), with Chinese commit messages such as 'default save_config does not restart the device'. So the Tiertime HS line very likely runs a Klipper-derived firmware from the vendor. (3) Moonraker is not shown to be there. The developer's moonraker and fluidd forks are untouched (0 commits ahead, last pushed 2023). Tiertime's official pages (UP300HS, UP600HS) name only 'UP Studio 3.0 / OrcaSlicer', a 'Linux System' touchscreen (UP600HS), USB/WiFi/Ethernet and a proprietary print queue. They never mention Klipper, Moonraker, Fluidd or Mainsail. Tiertime's historical network stack is its own WandServer, a WebSocket interface on port 3333. (4) No official Afinia spec page for the H+1(HS) could be found: afinia.com/h1hs returns 404, and the Afinia store lists only the QD330. There is no community mod that adds Moonraker. Conclusion: this is most likely a stock Klipper fork without Moonraker out of the box, but no official source confirms it. Under the rule to keep only printers that really run Klipper with Moonraker as the print host, it should stay UNCLEAR and not be kept as a Moonraker target until someone confirms it on a real unit. Note: my web search budget was used up, so the research relied on WebFetch and the GitHub API.

stock_firmware: Anycubic Kobra OS / GoKlipper (Go re-implementation) on Trigorilla Spe board
second_opinion: I could not refute it. The stock machine uses a Trigorilla Spe mainboard (SPE_A_V1.0.0) whose Allwinner R582-S3 ARM SoC controls the whole printer. It runs Anycubic's heavily modified, binary-packed Klipper derivative (Kobra OS / GoKlipper family), so it is not real Klipper and has no Moonraker. I found no real-Klipper firmware for the stock board. Rinkhals, the only established overlay, lists only Kobra 3 / 3 Max / 3 V2, Kobra 2 Pro (Trigorilla Spe B only), S1 and S1 Max. It does not list the Kobra 2 Max, and even on supported printers it keeps GoKlipper as the base and adds Moonraker/Mainsail on top. The Klipper Discourse threads say it is 'not (yet) possible to flash native Klipper to the stock mainboard of the Kobra 2 Max'. The only working path is replacing the mainboard, e.g. MKS Robin Nano v3.1 with a printables adapter plate, following the Klipper4Kobra2series configs. That is a hardware conversion, not a firmware mod of the stock printer, so it does not qualify as KLIPPER_VIA_ESTABLISHED_MOD. Confidence could be raised to medium-high. An optional note for the maintainer is the board-swap path (Discourse thread 'Anycubic Kobra 2 Pro/Plus/Max + MKS Robin Nano v3.1 = native Klipper').

second_opinion: I disagree with UNCLEAR. The researcher missed the vendor's own docs in the Hyvision/OrcaForCubicon repo (Hyvision makes Cubicon). The file cubicon/doc/build-volume-guard-firmware.md is titled "기종별 출력 제한 — 펌웨어(Klipper) 작업 문서", which means "per-model print limit: firmware (Klipper) work document". It hands the Cubicon firmware team printer.cfg edits for the xCeler-Mini, xCeler-I (250x250x290) and xCeler-Plus: [gcode_macro START_PRINT] checks REQ_X/Y/Z, uses action_raise_error, and needs a [respond] section. It also says Klipper macros ignore parameters they don't use, so older machines in the field won't break when they get the new slicer files. So the machines in the field run a Klipper printer.cfg with vendor macros. That makes the firmware stock Klipper (possibly vendor-patched), not Marlin. The OrcaSlicer profile agrees: gcode_flavor is klipper and the start G-code is START_PRINT EXTRUDER_TEMP/BED_TEMP. It overrides the Marlin default in the common Cubicon file. On Moonraker, the same doc says Moonraker and Mainsail handle UTF-8 but some LCD firmwares break Korean text, so messages should be in English. That points to a Moonraker/Mainsail stack alongside the LCD, but I found no spec page that confirms Moonraker is reachable out of the box. The octoprint host_type in the profile does not rule it out, because OrcaSlicer's OctoPrint host type also works against Moonraker. Confidence is high that the firmware is Klipper and medium that Moonraker is stock; the fallback would be STOCK_KLIPPER_NO_MOONRAKER. I could not reach the Cubicon website (3dcubicon.com shows a captcha and cubicon.com redirects to a parked domain), and the WebSearch budget was used up. mod_project: none needed.

Evidence I checked: (1) flashforge.com has no A5 product page. The obvious URLs return 404, and the Shopify products.json lists only the 5M and 5M Pro, so there is no vendor spec or firmware statement. (2) The established mods that put real Klipper and Moonraker on Flashforge machines do not list the A5. ZMOD covers FF5M/5M Pro/AD5X/Creator 5/Creator 5 Pro. Forge-X (DrA1ex/ff5m) and xblax's klipper mod cover only the AD5M (Pro). A search of GitHub issues found no A5 references either. So KLIPPER_VIA_ESTABLISHED_MOD cannot apply, and nothing confirms STOCK_KLIPPER_*. Caveat: this session's WebSearch budget ran out part-way. I did not search non-English or regional launch coverage, such as Chinese-market listings, which may exist. Re-check once Flashforge publishes an A5 spec or firmware page, or once ZMOD adds support. Until then, following the maintainer's rule to keep only verified Klipper printers, UNCLEAR (and therefore excluded) is correct.

second_opinion: I could not refute the claim. Two independent sources point to a modified Klipper on the stock firmware. First, a 3dprint.com reviewer found Klipper in the printer's logs. Second, a Klipper Discourse thread on a Flashforge license violation lists the Guider 3, 3 Plus and 3 Ultra among the Flashforge printers confirmed to run modified Klipper. Flashforge itself calls the firmware closed source and denies using Klipper code, so the evidence is mixed but leans toward Klipper. Moonraker does not ship stock. The printer talks through Flashforge's own network API and cloud. I searched GitHub and the wider web and found no established root or Klipper/Moonraker mod for the Guider 3 Ultra. Mods of that kind exist only for the AD5M (xblax), the Creator 5 (pappicio/ffc5) and the Adventurer 3 (SSH only). So moonraker='n/a' and an empty mod_project are correct. Because nothing puts Moonraker on this printer, it has no working path to Moonraker, which is the only print host. Under the maintainer's rule it should not be offered as a Moonraker print host, even though its firmware is Klipper-based. second_opinion: UNCLEAR is too cautious. LONGER's own downloads show the LK10 runs Klipper out of the box. (1) LONGER's official sample G-code for the LK10 (Drive folder linked from longer.net/pages/download-lk10, sliced with the vendor's OrcaSlicer profile) has 'gcode_flavor = klipper'. It uses commands only Klipper understands: EXCLUDE_OBJECT_DEFINE/START/END, SET_VELOCITY_LIMIT ACCEL_TO_DECEL/SQUARE_CORNER_VELOCITY, and custom Klipper macros (START_PRINT_PREPARE, START_PRINT_COOL_PURGE, START_PRINT_FINAL_HEAT). It also has 'host_type = octoprint', 'printer_model = LONGER LK10'. (2) The official LK10 user manual (spec table) lists LAN + WiFi. Chapter 'Connect the LK10 to OrcaSlicer' says: 'Select "Octo/Klipper" as the host type, enter the IP address ... click "Test"'. So there is a network host API reachable out of the box with no root. OrcaSlicer's Octo/Klipper host is the one used for Moonraker, which answers it through its OctoPrint-compatible API. (3) Product page: 'Klipper High-Speed Board'. Caveat: no LONGER document names Moonraker, Mainsail or Fluidd explicitly. The host could in theory be a vendor shim that only mimics the OctoPrint API, so the Moonraker part is inferred, not documented. Confidence is medium: Klipper itself is high, Moonraker is medium. If strict Moonraker proof is required, fall back to STOCK_KLIPPER_NO_MOONRAKER pending a hardware check (port 7125 / /server/info). NOT_KLIPPER and UNCLEAR are both refuted. Web search budget was exhausted, so community/Reddit confirmation was not possible. No GitHub repos for the LK10 exist, so there is also no mod project.

The vendor URL is empty locally, and PR #15796 only pointed it at orcaslicer.com. So no real machine exists that runs Klipper, and the rule "keep only printers that really run Klipper" excludes it.

The researcher's reasoning is partly wrong, though. It says the profile stands for Bambu X1C hardware running Bambu firmware, but the local profile says otherwise. In resources/profiles/OrcaArena/machine/fdm_bbl_3dp_001_common.json, the base preset that 'Orca Arena X1 Carbon 0.4 nozzle' inherits from sets "gcode_flavor": "klipper". So it is a Klipper-flavored reference profile that borrows Bambu-style file names, bed and hotend models, not a Bambu machine profile.

That does not make it a real Klipper printer. It is not a DIY design either (there are no build docs or BOM), and no mod project applies to hardware that does not exist.
